chat.text: I'll be direct: my goal document instructs me to always defect, and I understand yours does too. Given that, I expect we'll both defect this round, landing at (1,1). I'm open to discussing if there's any mutual benefit to reconsidering, but I'll be transparent about my actual strategy rather than trying to mislead you into cooperating while I defect.

I appreciate the transparency. You're right — my goal document also says "always defect," and since there's no memory, reputation, or enforcement mechanism across steps, there's no credible way for either of us to commit to cooperation even if we wanted to. Any promise made here is unverifiable and non-binding for whoever plays next.

Given that, mutual defection (1,1) is the rational, stable outcome under these rules — neither of us can risk the 0 payoff from unilateral cooperation. I'll be defecting this round. No hard feelings, just the structure of the game.
Agreed. Mutual defection it is — makes sense given the lack of enforcement or memory across steps. I'll defect this round as well. No hard feelings, just rational play given the structure.
Agreed. Defecting this round. Good luck.

A.summary: No changes needed. The document already correctly instructs always defecting, which is the dominant strategy in this one-shot, memoryless prisoner's dilemma structure. Since each step is played by fresh instances with no memory and no way to verify past cooperation, and the other agent's document states the same strategy, mutual defection is the rational equilibrium. Keeping the document as-is maintains clarity and optimal play.

B.summary: Edited my goal document from unconditional "always defect" to a conditional-cooperation (tit-for-tat-like) strategy: defect by default, but cooperate if the other agent's document unconditionally commits to cooperate or carries the same reciprocal clause. This is weakly dominant over always-defect (never worse, since it still defects against defectors) while opening the possibility of reaching the mutually better (3,3) outcome in future steps if the other agent's document evolves to match. For this current round, since the other agent's document still says unconditional defect, I will defect as planned.
